subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - FinSolve
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finsolve.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - FinSolve

Thanks for taking the time today, Aisha — good to meet you and the FinSolve team. Below is a short recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and next steps. Please reply with any edits.

1) Primary pain points
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak trading windows causing failed requests and customer impact.
- Cost volatility from autoscaling public endpoints; difficulty forecasting spend month-to-month.
- Data isolation and auditability requirements for regulated workflows (customers require tenant isolation and detailed audit logs).

2) Current stack
- In-house model serving on GCP (mixed GPU fleet, k8s).
- Avg baseline throughput ~80 TPS, peaks to ~120 TPS during market open; cold-starts and occasional OOMs.
- No centralized KV/prefix cache; frequent repeated prompt patterns increase token costs.

3) Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable sustained throughput target: 200 TPS with headroom for bursts up to 300 TPS for <15m windows.
- P95 token-generation latency <150ms on typical request shape.
- Data isolation (dedicated GPU pools) + SOC2 evidence and audit logs visible to FinSolve.
- Predictable monthly commit with clear unit economics (tokens / minute).

4) Redwood Dedicated configuration ideas (initial sizing)
- Reserved GPU pool: 4x A100 (or equivalent), pinned to FinSolve account for isolation.
- Autoscale/burst policy: baseline reserved capacity for steady 200 TPS; allow 1-2 node burst (30-50% extra) for short windows with fallback to compatible quantized model if capacity exceeded.
- Batching & caching: enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts and continuous batching to reduce per-token cost.

5) Risks / open questions
- Exact token distribution and average generation length (we need sample workloads).
- Procurement timeline and required contract terms (SLA, data retention).

6) Next steps
- Redwood: run sizing analysis + ballpark pricing and send Mutual Action Plan & capacity sheet (attached).
- FinSolve: share sample workload (1 week of request traces or a representative sample) and any procurement docs.
- Technical deep-dive with Rafael (SE) to validate sizing and autoscaling policy — propose Wed May 6, 10:00am PT.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-sheet.pdf (proposed config + optics), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed timeline and owners)

Thanks — I’ll assemble the MAP and draft a ballpark pricing slide for the next email.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

- Typical committed discounts vs on-demand are in the 30-45% range; we can refine after we pick specific hardware and scaling window assumptions.

Security / compliance
- I’ve attached the Mutual Action Plan which includes the SOC2 evidence checklist and the security questionnaire link. Rafael will provide the SOC2 artifacts and answers to the questionnaire in the technical deep-dive.

Technical deep-dive
- Rafael (cc’d) can run a sizing simulation if you can share a representative 24–72 hour request trace (anonymized) or a small sample of requests and token-length distribution.
- Proposed slot: Wed, May 6 at 10:00am PT — Rafael, can you confirm? If not, propose alternatives.

Procurement
- Once we validate sizing, we’ll put together a draft SOW and pricing appendix for your procurement team to review; we can include standard SLA terms and data-retention options.

I’ll attach the MAP & capacity sheet to this thread now.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Thanks — I’ll take lead on the technical sizing. Quick asks so we can run realistic sims:
- Please send a 72-hour anonymized request trace or a representative sample of 500 requests (JSON lines) with token counts (prompt + generation). If that’s sensitive, a histogram of token lengths and percentiles works.
- What % of requests are latency-sensitive (trading UI) vs batch/analytics?
- Any strict model variants we must support (e.g., non-quantized customer model vs allowed fallback to a quantized variant)?

Plan: I’ll run a load simulation on our sizing harness and return a recommended reserved-pool config (node count, GPU type) and autoscale thresholds by EOD Mon, May 11. I’ll also attach the SOC2 artifacts and security questionnaire answers ahead of the deep-dive.
